name: A Rose Is Still a Rose

info.album: A Rose Is Still A Rose

podcast.body: Released in the same month as her 1998 Grammys performance, this single cracked the pop top 30 and went top 5 on the R&B chart, featuring a collaboration with rapper Lauren Hill. Franklin told biographer Mark Bego that she was more excited about its chart performance than her impromptu "Nessun Dorma" rendition. "The same month she did that killer 1998 Grammys performance, she dropped a single wheel discuss later that cracked the pop top 30, went top 5 on the R&B chart, and paired her with rapper Lauren Hill."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Say a Little Prayer Edition Part 1

podcast.body: Written and produced by Lauryn Hill, who also sang on the chorus, this song was bequeathed to Franklin and expertly blended her classic sound, echoing hits like "(You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman" and "Spanish Harlem," with a loping hip hop beat characteristic of 1998. It subtly interpolated Edie Brickell & New Bohemians' "What I Am," and peaked at number 26 on the Hot 100 and number 5 on the R&B Hip Hop Songs Chart, becoming Franklin's last top 40 hit of her lifetime. "The song deftly pulled off several tricks at once. A Rose is still a Rose sounded like Aritha, echoing prior hits of hers like a natural woman or Spanish Harlem. But it also sounded like 1998 with a loping hip hop beat."
